title: Select Cross-Vendor Collaborators by Empirically Complementary Error Profiles
target_platform: Multi-vendor CLI agent pool (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google); evaluating-agent-work; usage telemetry (ceiling 1.2M tokens)
hypothesis: A team selector trained on development-set error patterns will achieve >= 8 percentage points higher task success than the strongest preregistered control (best individual model repeated sampling, random cross-vendor teams, fixed asymmetric roles) while staying within the same measured inference-cost ceiling.
falsification_criteria: Fail if the advantage is below 8 points, exceeds the cost ceiling, or disappears on untouched task families. Selection using held-out answers invalidates the experiment. Vendor diversity is not assumed to be epistemic independence.
experiment: Collect blinded outputs from fixed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google endpoints on 80 development problems. Estimate complementary errors by task class. Freeze selection rules and evaluate 120 held-out problems. Keep aggregation rules constant across arms so the experiment isolates team selection.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Frontier models are explicitly evaluated as team participants; total experiment ceiling is 1.2M tokens.

related_missions.MISSION-013: EXTENDS: replaces arbitrary role assignments with empirically measured error complementarity.
related_missions.MISSION-035: CONSUMES: relies on real-time measured token and quota telemetry across vendor backends.
related_missions.MISSION-033: SUPPLIES DATA TO: guides dynamic worker selection during parallel mission orchestrations.
related_missions.MISSION-051: SUPPLIER: per-model effort ratios on a shared size bucket (criterion c), the measured complementarity data this mission needs.

resources: three bounded backend cloud quotas (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google); ceiling 1.2M tokens
